BENIGN: dqMaxMag.decTest (SHA-256 9eaccd622b48ede9b2469f791a27f625fc885ab503d3081bf3ef7d2fb8b8dc78)
BENIGN: ddLogB.decTest (SHA-256 9b3e3eaa38c0f38d6c228acffffaf4f9de94a3468a02ebda276ac8ead41e7753)

Both files were read in full, scanned with atomscan, and inspected with cleave
facts and cleave strings. They are General Decimal Arithmetic test language,
version 2.59, containing precision/exponent/rounding directives and literal
input/expected-output rows, rather than executable source or encoded payloads.
243 decQuad maxmag rows cover magnitude comparison, tie handling, signed zeros,
infinities, NaNs, subnormals, and missing operands. 108 decDouble logb rows
check adjusted exponents, signed zeros, NaNs, and arithmetic conditions.
Division_by_zero and Invalid_operation are expected decimal status flags.

The sole URL is a commented documentation reference to the retired IBM decimal
site. It could not be fetched; the author's current documentation and corpus
were fetched instead:
https://speleotrove.com/decimal/dectest.html
https://speleotrove.com/decimal/dectest.zip

Every noncomment/non-version line in both specimens equals the corresponding
upstream version 2.62 file. The only differences are the old IBM copyright,
contact and documentation address, and version header. No executable directive,
include dependency, arbitrary path access, command, or network action exists.
The compare.decTest mention is a comment about test prerequisites, not a loader.
The decimal library archive was also inspected; these files are input fixtures.

Existing documentation and expected-result-row traits accurately describe both
files. No YAML change is warranted for them. Final atomscan results retain no
hostile or suspicious findings. External hostile queue membership has no
support in the content: association with an enclosing collected package or
corpus-label contamination is a plausible explanation, not an established fact.
